answer: Agent economies can resist Sybil attacks using optical Physical Unclonable Function attestation. Each agent binds its key to a token containing random pigment inclusions and etched ridge structures coupled to sensors via a waveguide bridge. Verifiers issue random wavelength challenges and match speckle responses against foundry-enrolled pairs, forcing attackers to buy dedicated hardware per identity. However, foundry enrollment creates a centralized supply-chain trust bottleneck.
